title.desc: Ask in plain English. Deckhand asks for what it needs, runs the calculation, and sends back a report you can keep.

turns.html: We're laying a 12-inch export line and I need to know if it'll stay put on the seabed in a storm — can you check on-bottom stability?

Happy to run that for you — a few things so I screen it the right way:
  • Pipe make-up — steel size and wall, plus coating (type, thickness) and contents (empty for install, or product-filled)?
  • Water depth, and your metocean for the return period — the near-bed wave velocity and the steady current?
  • Seabed soil — sand or clay, so I can set the pipe-soil friction?
I'll work the DNV-RP-F109 simplified lateral check. If you only have surface wave data I can flag that the near-bed velocity still needs deriving before the verdict stands.

12.75-inch steel, 0.5-inch wall, 80 mm concrete weight coat, empty for the install case. Bottom velocity 1.5 m/s with 0.52 m/s² near-bed acceleration for the 1-year storm, sandy seabed so friction 0.5. Details attached.

Got it — empty install case, sandy seabed. Basis I'll use: DNV-RP-F109 simplified lateral check — Morison drag + inertia + lift on the line, balanced against submerged weight and soil friction, with the normal safety-class factor of 1.1. Verdict holds when utilisation stays at or below 1.0. Running it now…

Here's how the line sits in the 1-year storm:
QuantityValueVerdict
Submerged weight2.13 kN/m—
Horizontal load (drag + inertia)0.72 kN/m—
Lateral utilisation0.96✅ Stable · 4% margin
Required submerged weight2.08 kN/mhave 2.13 kN/m
It holds, but only just — 4% of margin on the 80 mm coat. If the storm return period or current firms up, a thicker weight coat would buy headroom.

report.title: On-Bottom Stability (DNV-RP-F109)
report.inputs:
Pipe
12.75-inch steel · OD 323.9 mm · wall 12.7 mm
80 mm concrete weight coat (ρ 3040 kg/m³) · empty (install case)
Total OD over coat 483.9 mm

Metocean (1-year storm)
near-bed velocity 1.5 m/s · acceleration 0.524 m/s²
seawater 1025 kg/m³

Hydrodynamic + soil
Cd 0.7 · Cm 3.29 · Cl 0.9 · pipe-soil friction μ 0.5
Safety-class factor γ 1.1 (normal)
report.methodology:
1 · Submerged weight Ws = dry weight (steel + concrete coat) − displaced-seawater buoyancy, per metre.
2 · Hydrodynamic loads from Morison — drag 0.5·ρ·Cd·D·U|U|, inertia ρ·Cm·(π/4)·D²·a, lift 0.5·ρ·Cl·D·U².
3 · Lateral check, DNV-RP-F109 §4.3.2 simplified form: utilisation = γ·F_H ÷ (μ·(Ws − F_L)).
4 · Required weight to reach utilisation = 1.0: Ws = γ·F_H ÷ μ + F_L.
5 · Verdict: line is stable when utilisation ≤ 1.0.
report.outputs:
QuantityValue
Dry weight3.98 kN/m
Buoyancy1.85 kN/m
Submerged weight Ws2.13 kN/m
Drag0.39 kN/m
Inertia0.32 kN/m
Horizontal load F_H0.72 kN/m
Lift F_L0.50 kN/m
Lateral utilisation0.96
Required submerged weight2.08 kN/m
Verdict: STABLE — utilisation 0.96 ≤ 1.0; the 80 mm weight coat clears the 1-year storm with about 4% margin. Have 2.13 kN/m against 2.08 kN/m required.
